items.text: Before each release of my Excel add-in I walk through a list of what every button is supposed to do, so each release gets the same check.
When something broke I dug through the server error logs in Kibana and attached the log lines to the bug report so developers could see what happened.
I set it up so that pushing a version tag builds the Android app, signs it, and publishes it and the web app without anyone doing it by hand.
Every change to my site starts as a GitHub issue, goes through a pull request, and only merges once the build passes.
I tested checkout with every major credit card brand across the 3D Secure, address, and security code combinations.
I stood up a stand-in for the company intranet server on Windows Server so I could try web parts safely, resetting it every week from a snapshot.
I fix guitars and amplifiers for customers, adjusting the setup and re-soldering broken connections while they wait.
I moved a couple dozen old reports onto a new data source, which cut down on numbers that did not match.
We ran the music festival cheaply so more local bands got heard and the leftover money went to charity.
Before shipping, I install the new app version over the old one and check that saved recordings and boards still work.
My sourdough starter needs feeding twice a day and the crust came out too pale last weekend.
It rained all afternoon, so the picnic moved indoors and we played cards until the sun came back.
The tomato plants in the back garden need staking before the next windy week.
